newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Short-dated FX vols soft, yen skew stays.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short-dated FX vols soft, yen skew stays.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options softened, particularly in the shorter maturities, as the spot dollar firmed, dealers said.

Dollar/yen risk reversals, the put/call pricing differential, remained sharply skewed for yen calls despite a bounce of more than one yen in the dollar to the mid-114 yen area, which depressed volatilities as a whole, they added.
Dollar/mark volatilities failed to pick up, despite a spot rally toward 1.74 marks, just short of recent highs.
"Volatilities are all moving lower," said Ted Voorhees, a senior trader at Deutsche Bank in New York.
One-month dollar/mark implied volatility stood at 7.9/8.2 percent in late trade, down from Thursday's 8.2/8.5 percent.

Voorhees said the pressure might have come from long positions in the upper strike prices, which had become rich in theta -- the rate of time decay -- after today's rally in spot, or perhaps from exotic option positions.
"Gamma is being sold for whatever reason," he noted. "The front end is being sold aggressively. In the back end, though, there's some demand for low-delta options. That's keeping support for vega."

Shorter-dated options have higher gamma, which provides bigger swings in delta for volatility traders as well as quicker premium acceleration but also entails steeper time decay. Longer-dated options have higher vega, the rate of premium change per incremental move in spot.
Dollar/Swiss franc volatilities also stayed subdued, despite a fairly impressive rally past recent minor peaks near 1.45 francs. Trading was thin after the London market closed.
Spreads between dollar/mark volatilities and dollar/Swiss remained at about 1.3 point in the front end and 1.8 in the back end, a European bank trader in Chicago said.
In dollar/yen the steeply inverted volatility curve flattened as the front end, sensitive to spot rates as well as time decay, tumbled after the dollar's bounce overnight.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen stood at 10.8/11.1 percent, down from a high trade of 12.0 on Thursday.

However, bid for downside yen calls refused to wane. One-month 25-delta was quoted at 2.2/2.5 point in favor of yen calls in late trade, little changed from Thursday. Earlier in Europe it was said to have traded as high as 2.75.
"They're as bid as they ever have been," the Chicago trader said.
MaryBeth Slack, FX options analyst at MCM OptionWatch, said low-delta yen puts were also starting to see interest but were dwarfed by the demand for yen calls.
She said yen calls were so expensive that buyers were forced to partially fund the purchase with put selling.
"We haven't seen much in the way of straight, outright call buying -- it's all been in risk reversals," Slack said.

"People are going out the (maturity) curve and in on the vol smile (curve), because the volatility smile has become so sharp from the demand of low-delta risk reversals," she said. A smile curve shows the volatilities of different strikes.
-- Shin Kishima/Chicago Derivatives Desk ((312-408-8750))
E-mail: derivatives@reuters.com
